thread:
alex_ng: @channel customer X reporting >20% 504s from hosted inference in eu-west-1 starting ~15:32 UTC. They say requests timeout after ~12s. Seeing large error spike in our alerts. Anyone oncall? :exclamation:

maria_s: I'm on it. Do we have a correlation with scale events / KEDA?

sre_oncall: Diving in. Quick checks: gateway 504s, backend rows show high queue depth on inference-service-pool, pods going from 0->1 frequently. Could be slow model init + scale-up lag.

support_jen: Customer provided sample trace ids: trace-xyz-1, trace-xyz-2. They saw retries too. Ticket: INC-7894.

infra_ben: Pulling autoscale logs now. KEDA scaler saw external metric spikes but scale-up didn't complete due to readiness probe failures. Logs show container restarted during init: "model load timeout".

deploy-bot: deploy/v1 inference-deployment scaled to 0 -> 1 replicas (trigger: keda-external) at 2023-09-24T15:31:45Z.

alex_ng: Repro strategy — simulate a burst to the route with a canary deployment and watch HPA/KEDA triggers. But first, mitigation for the customer? Suggest we enable reserved pool for the route or increase minReplicas.

maria_s: I pushed a temporary patch to the ScaledObject: set minReplicaCount: 1 and increased cooldownPeriod. Command I used: 
```
kubectl patch scaledobject inference-so -n prod --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":1,"cooldownPeriod":300}}'
```
This should prevent coldstart for 5m while we investigate.

sre_oncall: Good. Also lowering readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds to 5 won't help if model init is long; we should increase initialDelaySeconds so K8s doesn't treat slow init as failure. Current readiness is 10s and probe fails causing restart loops.

infra_ben: Observed model init logs: 
```
[2023-09-24T15:31:46Z] INFO model-loader: starting weights download
[2023-09-24T15:32:00Z] WARN model-loader: slow fetch (s3): 12.3s
[2023-09-24T15:32:12Z] ERROR model-loader: init timeout (limit 15s) -> exit(1)
```
So container exits after 15s, restarts, and KEDA scales based on request queue, but pods never become ready fast enough.

support_jen: Customer says they had a short burst due to a retry storm from their side after a downstream error, so traffic spiked.

alex_ng: Root cause hypothesis: aggressive KEDA external-scaler + low minReplicas + short model init timeout + readiness probe misconfig -> scale-up thrash leading to gateway 504s.

maria_s: Agreed. Two-pronged fix: short-term: keep minReplicaCount=1 for affected service and add a prewarm job to keep one model instance loaded; long-term: increase model init timeout and implement background pre-warming for heavy models.

sre_oncall: Repro steps I ran locally (notes):
1) Deploy inference replica with model X and set replicas=0.
2) Send 200 concurrent requests over 10s to route /v1/generate.
3) Observe KEDA external metric spike, scaler fires, HPA requests new pod, pod init logs show model fetch, container crashes on init timeout -> gateway 504s for ~60s.

Commands used: 
```
# simulate burst
ab -n 200 -c 200 https://hosted.redwood.example/v1/generate
# inspect scaledobject
kubectl get scaledobject inference-so -n prod -o yaml
# check pods
kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference -o wide
```

infra_ben: Temporary patch we pushed to decrease restart loops: increased model init timeout ENV var MODEL_INIT_TIMEOUT=120 and set readinessProbe.periodSeconds=10 and failureThreshold=12. Patch command: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/inference --namespace=prod MODEL_INIT_TIMEOUT=120
kubectl patch deploy inference -n prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/failureThreshold","value":12}]'
```
Should reduce restarts so pod gets to ready state.

sre_oncall: After changing minReplicas and env, customer 504 rate dropped from 21% -> 3% over next 4 minutes. But we still see occasional slow responses at tail ~2s extra.

maria_s: Follow-ups:
- Add a dedicated reserved pool for large models (Redwood Dedicated-style) as an opt-in for customers with heavy cold-start sensitive workloads.
- Add an automated prewarm hook when KEDA sees an external spike (create a standby pod without killing it).
- Improve docs for customers about retry/backoff so they don't amplify spikes.

support_jen: I'll update the customer: applied emergency mitigation (minReplica=1 + increased init timeout). Requesting them to test and confirm.

alex_ng: Good. Ticket pointers and next steps:
- INC-7894: Incident record with timeline and mitigations applied.
- Follow-up task: ENG-1202 (prewarm support), ENG-1203 (improve scaler safeguards).

deploy-bot: rollout status deployment/inference: 1 updated replica(s) available.

infra_ben: Leaving the temporary minReplicaCount change in place for another 6 hours while we monitor. Will revert to 0 overnight if traffic is low.

sre_oncall: Monitoring dashboard: watch queue length, pod readiness, and model-loader error rates. I’ll keep this thread updated.

maria_s: Thanks team. Great catch on the readiness/probe interplay with KEDA.

support_jen: Customer confirmed reduced errors and will hold open until EOD. Marking current state: mitigated, monitoring. :white_check_mark:\"
